question: Does keying the BF16 prefill oracle per INT8 layer for multi-chunk packed calls restore agreement with the scalar-bulk parent, and what does it cost?
answer: Yes. Generated IDs match the parent exactly at 2 and 8 chunks. Speed is neutral (449.16 -> 451.71 tok/s at 2 chunks; 67.2 -> 67.31 at 8). Cost is a transient peak increase of ~0.94 GiB at 16,384 declared positions, scaling with declared context.
change: _int8_prefill_oracle_cache_for_layer keys the oracle per layer when the session's _int8_prefill_oracle_per_layer flag is set. _prefill_batch_native_impl sets it once per call, before the first slab, when len(chunks) > 1; prefill_batch_native's finally clears it with the oracle release. The scalar bulk (layer-outer) executor is untouched and keeps the shared pair.

protocol.prompt: deterministic varied prompt, numpy default_rng(20260909), token IDs in [1000, 32000)
protocol.kv: int8_per_token_head, FP32 per-token/head scales, max_sequence_length 16384 (route int8_direct, no mirror)
protocol.control: pre-fix arm measured by restoring the file to HEAD in the same session and rerunning

scalar_bulk_parent_ids_deterministic.note: 8192-row scalar IDs identical across the pre-fix and post-fix runs, so ID matching is a sound oracle here

1024_rows_1_chunk.note: unaffected; single-chunk calls keep the shared pair

8192_rows_8_chunks.note: residual logit delta with identical IDs is fp reassociation between the two executors

cost.mechanism: 15 additional BF16 oracle pairs; each pair is _int8_prefill_oracle_capacity_positions * head_count_kv * key_length * 2 * 2 bytes
cost.scaling_caveat: the oracle is sized by max(max_positions, backing_pages * block_size) - the whole pool - not the request's prompt length, so this cost grows with declared context and will lower long-context ceilings. Reclaiming it needs either the layer-outer packed executor or a logically-indexed oracle.

not_a_perf_claim: The 8-chunk packed rate (67 tok/s vs the scalar parent's 692) is a pre-existing chunk-count-driven slowdown, unchanged by this fix (67.2 before, 67.31 after). It is the per-slab whole-history import recorded as an open review finding, not attributable to this change.
